resources.string: Engine
Recognition engine
How the keyboard turns speech into text

The system recognizer is fast and shows the words while you speak, but it depends on the operating system and its languages. Offline Whisper runs fully on your device across many languages and sends no audio anywhere. It transcribes each phrase after you stop speaking. A transcription server does the same work on a computer you choose, so your phone spends less battery. The recording of each phrase goes to that server and nowhere else.
System recognizer
Offline Whistle
Fast, and it shows the words while you speak. It depends on your device and its languages
Cactus Whistle transcribes English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, and Polish on this device. Other languages use Android’s system recognizer.
Transcription server
Sends each phrase to a server you run, which saves battery. Each phrase arrives after you stop
Dictation
Voice typing view
What the microphone button opens

The panel gives large controls and status in the space of the keyboard. The compact bar speaks over the keys, so you can correct words as they land. The collapsed bar hides the whole keyboard behind a small pill that you can drag anywhere, and it stays until you bring the keyboard back. The panel and the compact bar have a collapse button, and the pill has an expand button, so you can switch styles without coming back to this screen.

Voice typing mode
How voice typing and the keys share the field

One block at a time is the usual way. The words appear in the field while you speak, and the first key press stops the microphone.

Type while you speak keeps the microphone open. Each phrase goes into the field when you stop for breath, so the keys, the layouts and the suggestion strip stay live all through the session. Use it with the compact bar over the keys. This mode always keeps listening.

Plain text works the same way, but it adds no punctuation and no spaces. You control all of them from the keyboard. Use it for code, for terminals and for any field where you want only the words you said.

Keep listening
Start the next sentence automatically after each one goes into the field
Stop after a pause
End a Whisper or server clip by itself when you stop talking

Offline Whisper and the transcription server record a whole clip, so the microphone stays open until you press it or the 30 second clip fills. Set a pause here and the clip ends by itself once you have said something and then gone quiet for that long. With Keep listening off, that also ends dictation, so you never have to reach for the microphone. The system recognizer stops after a pause of its own and ignores this. Off by default.

Transcription server
Server address
For example http://192.168.1.10:8000/v1. The keyboard adds /audio/transcriptions
Endpoint path
Optional. For a server with its own route, such as /v1/transcribe. It is added to the address as typed. Leave it empty to use /audio/transcriptions
Model
Optional. For example Systran/faster-whisper-small or whisper-large-v3-turbo
API key
Optional. Leave it empty for a server that needs no key
Send the keyboard language
Tell the server which language you are typing in. Turn this off to let the server detect it
Prompt
Optional. Text the model reads as what came before, to set spelling and style. Whisper models read only about the last 150 words of it
Words to listen for
Listen for my words
Names and other words from your dictionary, so they are spelled your way

Each time you dictate, the keyboard sends a list of your own words with it: the words you added by hand, the words in Android\'s personal dictionary, and the words the keyboard learned from your typing that are not in any word list, such as names. The system engine also gets permission to use what it knows about your phone, such as your contacts. The list goes to the engine that listens to your voice, and nowhere else. The system engine uses it on Android 13 and later, if the engine supports it. A transcription server gets it as part of its prompt. Offline Whisper cannot use a list, so this setting does not show for it.
More words to listen for
Optional. Separate them with commas. These go first, before the words from your dictionary
Per language
Some models are better at some languages. Give a language its own model on the same server, or a server of its own. Dictation follows the language of the layout you are typing on.

The server answered. Voice typing is ready

Recognition uses the speech recognizer of your device. On Android 12 and later it runs on your device when the language model is installed. If it is not, the audio goes to the recognizer service while you speak. Press and hold the microphone to speak in walkie-talkie style. It stops when you let go.
Pause media during voice typing
Pause music and video while the microphone listens

When voice typing starts, the keyboard asks other apps to pause their sound. Music, podcasts and video stop while the microphone listens. They continue a moment after voice typing stops. An app that ignores the request continues to play.
Hold the tool to pick a mode
Press and hold the Voice tool on the toolbar to choose a voice typing mode and start at once

A press and hold on the toolbar\'s Voice tool opens a menu of the three voice typing modes. Picking one makes it the mode and starts dictation straight away, so switching between one block at a time and typing while you speak is one hold rather than a trip through settings. Tap the tool to stop. Turn this off to give the hold back to the toolbar: it then runs the tool you bound to it, or opens this screen.
Hold to talk
How long you hold the microphone before it becomes press-and-hold

A short tap on the microphone starts dictation and leaves it running until you tap again. Holding it instead dictates only while you hold, like a walkie-talkie. This is the line between the two. Raise it if a slow press keeps stopping your dictation, lower it if you mean to hold and it keeps latching on.
